name: The Forgotten Pools
summary: At the Forgotten Pools, life rises in the Barrens for reasons the Cenarion Circle cannot explain. Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads asks Horde adventurers to inspect the oasis northwest of the settlement, where druids feel unseen forces stirring below the earth.

sections.title: Stirrings in the Savannah
sections.body: Long ago, the Barrens flourished as fertile land. Ages of war and the Sundering shattered the continent and left this region a sun-baked scrubland. Now lush oases are taking root in its dry basin. The Cenarion Circle’s druids find this sudden growth unnatural. They feel powers below the earth pressing upward and stirring plants and wildlife to life in scattered pockets across the wastes.

sections.title: The Murky Depths
sections.body: Tonga Runetotem sends you to the Forgotten Pools, northwest of the Crossroads, to learn more about the new growth. Beneath the water, a fissure vents strange gases that bubble into the pool. Tonga cannot yet say what it means. Still, the fissure gives him a tangible clue as the Barrens changes around you.

faq.answer: Tonga Runetotem is a tauren druid of the Cenarion Circle stationed at the Crossroads. He studies the strange changes in the Barrens and seeks the reason oases are appearing across its dry plains.

faq.q: Why is the Cenarion Circle investigating the Forgotten Pools?
aliases: what is wrong with the pools
faq.answer: The Cenarion Circle investigates because its druids feel concentrated energy forcing life to the surface. They seek the power feeding the new oases before it grows beyond control.

faq.q: What is found at the bottom of the Forgotten Pools?
faq.answer: An underwater fissure vents bubbling gases into the pool. Tonga thinks it may reveal the force rising to the surface, though he cannot yet be sure.

faq.q: Where are the Forgotten Pools located?
faq.answer: The Forgotten Pools lie northwest of the Crossroads in the central Barrens. Palms and water mark the oasis amid the dry land.

faq.q: Was the Barrens always a desert?
faq.answer: No. Druidic lore says the Barrens was once lush and full of life. Ancient wars and cataclysms scorched the land, leaving the arid savannah seen today.

faq.q: What comes after investigating the Forgotten Pools?
aliases: what to do after forgotten pools
faq.answer: Tonga Runetotem sends you southeast to inspect another Barrens oasis, the Stagnant Oasis.

angles.text: As a druid, you witness the Cenarion Circle watching the strange forces changing the Barrens’ natural growth.
As a tauren, you know the Barrens matters to the nomadic tribes of the Earth Mother. Its water sources matter to tauren travelers, who must understand and preserve them.
As a member of the Horde, you have reason to safeguard the water near the Crossroads, where roads meet between Durotar, Mulgore, and Ashenvale.
